title: The Prosocial Ranking Challenge: Reducing Polarization on Social Media without Sacrificing Engagement
abstract: arXiv:2603.19626v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We report the first direct comparisons of multiple alternative social media algorithms on multiple platforms on outcomes of societal interest. We used a browser extension to modify which posts were shown to desktop social media users, randomly assigning 9,386 users to a control group or one of five alternative ranking algorithms which simultaneously altered content across three platforms for six months during the US 2024 presidential election. This reduced our preregistered index of affective polarization by an average of 0.03 standard deviations (p < 0.05), including a 1.5 degree decrease in differences between the 100 point inparty and outparty feeling thermometers. translated_title: 亲社会排名挑战：在不牺牲参与度的情况下减少社交媒体上的极化
translated_abstract: 我们报告了首个在多个平台上对多种替代社交媒体算法在社会关注结果上的直接比较。我们使用浏览器扩展来修改桌面社交媒体用户看到的帖子，随机将9,386名用户分配到对照组或五种替代排名算法之一，这些算法在2024年美国总统大选期间同时改变了三个平台上的内容，持续六个月。这使得我们预先注册的情感极化指数平均减少了0.03个标准差（p < 0.05），包括100点党内和党外情感温度计差异降低了1.5度。我们观察到Facebook（-0.37分钟/天）和Reddit（-0.2分钟/天）的活跃使用时间减少，但X/Twitter的使用时间增加了0.32分钟/天（p < 0.01）。我们还看到负面社交媒体体验的报告增加，但未发现对幸福感、新闻知识的影响。
tldr: 本研究通过大规模随机实验，首次证明替代排名算法能有效降低社交媒体上的情感极化，同时保持用户参与度基本稳定。
en_tdlr: This study, through a large-scale randomized experiment, provides the first evidence that alternative ranking algorithms can effectively reduce affective polarization on social media while maintaining user engagement.
